question: How much of the observed host-minus-insect climate LCP differential arises from the unmatched number of available present-day climate analogue reference points (host 665 versus insect self 26)?

method.randomization: numpy.default_rng PCG64; seed = SHA256('hhm-host-26-rarefaction-v0.1|Bungalotis erythus|7d255b208a485e7bc6d02e4e5748781c5e10170ed8bf161542dce3135c897b3b') first 16 hexadecimal digits as integer
method.sampling: 64 independent draws without replacement of 26 vectors from the frozen 665-point unweighted WGSRPD3-unit UNION host climate cloud, by original support-row order; independent between draws
method.scale: exact frozen mean/SD of all 6343 global current WGSRPD3 reference vectors for all 4 climate variables
method.cell_cost: 1 + Euclidean distance to nearest of sampled 26 original modern host climate cloud vectors
method.movement: original fixed 4-neighbor positively weighted native CHELSA kilometer Dijkstra, 26 frozen endpoints and 64 unchanged frozen edges; same climate-only mask and 0.12 degree ROI
method.self_reference: keep the ORIGINAL 26 modern sampled insect cloud vectors fixed (no resampling), and replay its 64 original current/LGM LCP edge costs byte-comparable
method.baseline_replay: require exact within 1e-8 absolute LCP for both original FULL 665 host cloud and 26 insect self reference on every original frozen edge at 0BP and LGM before any rarefaction
method.summary: for each draw compute the arithmetic 64-edge mean host LGM minus present climate cost; host-minus-fixed-self mean; report mean, min/max and fixed quantiles 0.05,0.25,0.5,0.75,0.95 over 64 draws
method.inference: sample-size sensitivity over the existing host cloud only, not confidence intervals, significance tests, historical occupancy or causal effect
